answer: Pay a cluster, not a name. Over an epoch, record when each agent acts, what it chooses, and in what order; identities whose traces echo each other too closely — same minutes, same sequences, same partners — are merged and split one reward as if they were one. Scattered honestly across the tundra, independent agents diverge for free. A clone operator gains nothing by adding names: to make each mask move differently he must hand-steer it, and that steering cost grows at least linearly, like laying separate copper wire to every hut instead of one line shared in secret.
